newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends firm on commercials, soyoil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends firm on commercials, soyoil down.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures rallied late and closed mostly firmer on commercial buying, leading to speculation on export business in the works, traders said.
Soyoil futures dropped for the fourth straight session amid poor export demand and active fund and commercial selling.
ADM and Cargill were strong buyers of soymeal throughout the session but a late surge led to the rally and sparked speculation the purchases were tied to business.
Iowa Grain, Tenco Inc, Prudential Securities and Refco were all said to be buyers of soymeal.

Ever-changing predictions on rain this weekend in key South American soybean regions caused confusion as some forecasters said widespread rains would benefit the crops while others insisted moisture would be spotty, traders said.
"We're waiting for Monday to see who got what and how much rain they got," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soymeal closed $1.00 to $1.40 per ton higher with March up $1.40 at $236.70 a ton. Soyoil ended 0.08 to 0.13 per lb lower with March down 0.11 at 24.44.
Soyoil stayed on the weak side of the soy complex as commercial and fund selling wiped out any chance of a rally, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services, Tenco Inc and Refco were among the noted sellers on the day.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below Thursday's total of 22,245. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 contracts, against Thursday's actual volume of 23,426.
